title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Process, Runbooks, Rotations, and Templates
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook documents Redwood Inference's recommended on-call and incident response processes, runbook templates, postmortem guidance, rotation practices, game day exercises, and standard status-page / customer communications templates. It is intended to be a practical, operational reference for engineers, SREs, and incident commanders who execute and own incident management. Where appropriate the document provides concrete thresholds, steps, and sample text that teams should adopt or adapt.

Incident lifecycle (summary)

1. Detection — Alert triggers in our monitoring, user reports, or automated health checks indicate a potential incident.
2. Triage — On-call responder acknowledges and quickly assesses impact and scope.
3. Mitigation — Short-term actions to reduce customer impact (failover, throttling, scaling, rollback).
4. Resolution — Root cause addressed and service restored.
5. Recovery & Validation — Verify systems are healthy and monitor for regressions.
6. Post-incident review — Postmortem with action items and owners.

Severity definitions and thresholds

- Sev 1 (Critical): Service-wide outage or >50% of requests experiencing errors or latency beyond SLO for >5 minutes. Pager paging immediate.
- Sev 2 (High): Significant degradation affecting a major subset of customers or a core feature (e.g., model inference queue growth) for >15 minutes. Pager to primary on-call and secondary.
- Sev 3 (Medium): Localized failure affecting a small percentage of traffic or non-critical features. Alert to channel and follow-up by owner.
- Sev 4 (Low): Informational issues, minor issues, or tasks that can be handled during business hours.

Roles & responsibilities

- Primary on-call (Primary): First responder for incidents during rotation window. Responsible for initial triage, communication, and mitigation.
- Secondary on-call (Secondary): Backup to Primary, assists for escalations or if Primary is unavailable.
- Incident Commander (IC): Takes ownership of coordination for Sev1/2 incidents. Often the Primary initially; IC can be handed off.
- SRE Lead / Pager Duty Escalation (Escalation): For extended incidents or when broad platform changes are needed.
- Communications Lead: Prepares status page and customer communications with guidance from IC and product.
- Postmortem Owner: Responsible for coordinating the root cause analysis and tracking action items to completion.

Escalation matrix (example)

1. Primary on-call (ack within 3 minutes for Sev1).
2. If no response in 5 minutes or unable to mitigate, escalate to Secondary.
3. After 15 minutes without progress, escalate to SRE Lead.
4. For incidents impacting SLAs or legal/compliance concerns, notify Security and Legal teams immediately.

Initial triage checklist (first 10 minutes)

- Acknowledge alert and set incident severity.
- Capture initial impact: affected services, regions, % of traffic, customer-facing effects.
- Identify recent deploys or config changes (CI/CD window).
- Check capacity and autoscaling health (GPU pool, queue lengths).
- If degradation severe, perform one or more mitigations: failover to warm pool, enable degraded mode, throttle non‑critical routes, revert last deploy.
- Create incident channel (Slack) and post initial summary.

Runbook template (canonical)

Title: <service> — <symptom>
Scope: Short description of affected services and impact.
Symptoms / Alerts: Names of alerts, example metric thresholds, and sample alert text.
Detection steps: Commands and dashboards to verify the issue.
Mitigation steps (short-term): Step-by-step actions to reduce customer impact.
Root cause investigation: Key logs, traces, and places to check.
Resolution steps (long-term): Permanent fixes, rollout plan, and validation steps.
Owners: Primary runbook owner and escalation contacts.
Postmortem checklist: Items to capture for RCA.

Example runbook: inference-worker-high-latency

Title: inference-worker — high tail latency
Scope: A subset of GPU inference workers exhibiting >99th percentile latency > 3x baseline and increased error rates.
Symptoms / Alerts:
- alert: inference_worker_p99_latency > 1200ms for 5m
- alert: inference_error_rate > 2% for 5m

Detection steps:
1. Open dashboards: "Serving Runtime — Latency by cluster" and CPU/GPU utilization dashboards.
2. Query recent deploys: `git log --since="1 hour ago" --oneline` and check CI/CD pipeline window.

Quick mitigations:
- Scale up warm pool: `redwoodctl capacity scale --pool inference-warm --replicas +20`
- Evacuate problematic host: `k8s-cordon <node>` and `k8s-drain <node>`
- Enable degraded model: update routing policy to fallback smaller model variant (see routing playbook).

Investigation pointers:
- Check kernel-level OOMs and GPU driver logs at /var/log/nvidia/*.
- Inspect KV cache misses and prefix cache hit rates.
- Trace slow requests with trace id from the alert and open in Jaeger.

Rollout / resolution:
- If a recent deploy is implicated, roll back to previous stable tag: `deploy rollback <service> --tag <previous>`
- Deploy a patch with root cause fix and initiate gradual rollout (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%).
- Validate with canary traffic and observe p50/p95/p99 latency metrics for 30 minutes.

Postmortem & RCA process

- Timeline: Create a chronological timeline of events (detection, mitigation, changes, resolution).
- Evidence: Include logs, traces, dashboards, relevant commits, and config changes.
- Contributing factors: List technical and organizational factors.
- Root cause: Single-sentence root cause statement.
- Actions: Action items with owners, deadlines, and verification criteria.
- Severity review: Confirm the severity assigned was appropriate and document any reclassification.
- Publish: Postmortem must be published within 72 hours of incident resolution and shared to the company postmortem backlog.

Postmortem template (required fields)

- Title
- Incident ID
- Severity
- Summary (1–3 sentences)
- Timeline (timestamped)
- Impact (customers, SLOs, financial where applicable)
- Root cause
- Contributing factors
- Actions (owner, due date, verification)
- Prevention/monitoring changes (dashboards, alerts)
- Lessons learned

On-call rotations and schedules

- Primary rotation cadence: 1 week per engineer (Mon 00:00 UTC to next Mon 00:00 UTC) by default. Adjust per-team norms.
- Secondary rotation: two-week cadence, offset to ensure overlap with Primary.
- Holiday and on-call swaps: Use the on-call calendar in Google Calendar; all swaps must be recorded and acknowledged by both parties in the on-call rota spreadsheet.
- Handoffs: Primary should do a written handoff at shift start and end, including outstanding incidents and ongoing mitigations. Use Slack channel #oncall-handoffs for summaries.

Game days and readiness drills

Purpose: Validate runbooks, tooling, escalation paths, and communication templates under controlled conditions.
Frequency: Minimum quarterly for platform owners; annually for team-wide cross-functional drills.
Game day structure:
1. Announce non-technical participants and schedule.
2. Simulated incident injected (load test, component failure, or chaos test).
3. Run through detection, triage, mitigation, and comms.
4. Debrief and capture action items in the game day report.

Status page and customer communications

- Status page categories: Operational, Degraded, Partial Outage, Major Outage.
- Update cadence: Initial status within 15 minutes of a Sev1/Sev2 incident. Subsequent updates every 30 minutes until steady state, then hourly.
- Customer email template (initial):
Subject: Redwood Inference — Incident affecting [service-name]
Body:
We are investigating a [degraded / partial outage / outage] affecting [service-name]. Impact: [brief list of customer-visible symptoms]. We are currently mitigating and will provide an update by [time]. We apologize for the disruption and will share a full post-incident report.

- Status page sample entry:
Title: Major outage — [service-name]
Start time: 2026-02-10T15:12:00Z
Current status: Investigating
Updates:
- 15:20 UTC: Investigating - latency and errors have increased for a subset of customers.
- 15:45 UTC: Mitigation in progress - routing has been adjusted to fallback models for impacted customers.

Communication best practices:
- Keep messages concise, factual, and customer-oriented. Avoid technical jargon in initial customer-facing updates.
- Set expectations for timing, and avoid promising exact resolution times unless verified.
- Share root cause and remediation actions in the postmortem.

Operational tooling & integrations

- PagerDuty: Primary alerting and escalation. Policies must match Sev definitions above.
- Slack: Dedicated incident channels using standardized naming (incident-<id>-<service>). Archive channels after the postmortem is published.
- Runbook storage: Canonical runbooks live in the Confluence oncall runbooks folder and are referenced from PagerDuty alerts.
- Status page: Hosted by our StatusPage provider; integration with PagerDuty for automatic incident creation.
- CI/CD: Deploy rollbacks and canary tooling integrated with our internal `deploy` CLI.

SLOs and monitoring guidance

- Example SLO for hosted API: 99.9% successful requests per rolling 30d window with p95 latency < 250ms for small models; p95 < 450ms for large models.
- Alert guidance: Prefer SLO-based alerts for customer-impacting issues (error budget burn) and symptomatic alerts for infrastructure health.

Additional templates and quick references

- Slack incident channel join template:
`/msg @oncall Primary acknowledged. IC: <name>. Current severity: <sev>. Initial impact: <summary>. Next update: <time>`

- Incident close checklist:
1. Confirm system health and no regression for 60 minutes.
2. Post initial postmortem draft.
3. Notify customers (if impacted) with resolution and link to postmortem.
4. Close incident channel and tag messages for archive.

Appendix: Useful commands and dashboards

- `redwoodctl` commands for capacity and routing.
- Kibana queries for inference logs: `service:inference AND level:error AND @timestamp:[now-15m TO now]`
- Tracing service: Jaeger link pattern `https://jaeger.redwood.internal/trace/<trace-id>`

Ownership and review cadence

- Playbook owner: SRE manager. This document will be reviewed quarterly and after every Sev1 incident.
- Runbooks must be reviewed every 6 months and after any related incident.

Related documents

- Link to team-specific runbooks and the SLO definitions page.

Contact & escalation directory

- SRE Lead: Jon Martinez (pager: jon-martinez)
